title: We scanned 27,075 real developer prompts to ChatGPT and found 3 live API keys
summary: vendor publishes its own false-positive breakdown (1.12% alert rate, 48% of alerts a single noisy UUID rule) alongside the headline find, explicitly framing a benchmark that hides its noise as "marketing" — a runnable template for honest-benchmark posts

title: Jack Dorsey's Block launches Buzz, an open-source Slack+GitHub rival where AI agents get their own cryptographic identity
summary: founder-credibility launch drew real traffic (304 pts/258 comments on HN) but a skeptical verdict ("LLM slop," the irony of a GitHub-hosted GitHub-killer, Google Buzz comparisons) — a counter-case for the earned-distribution thread: reputation buys attention, not automatically the verdict

title: GitHub Code Quality moves from free preview to paid GA
summary: $10/committer/month plus usage-based AI consumption (Copilot review, Autofix), after 10,000+ enterprises ran it free in preview; HN barely blinked (4 pts, 0 comments) despite pricing a seat tax onto AI code review

title: New Copilot usage metrics impact dashboard
summary: GitHub now buckets enterprise Copilot seats into adoption-phase cohorts (Phase 1 code-first, Phase 2 agent-first, Phase 3 multi-agent/app, plus a "Passive" licensed-but-not-engaged segment) so admins can tell an impact story beyond raw seat activity

title: HCLTech: "The Blueprint for AI Leadership"
summary: 500-enterprise survey with Raconteur (published 2026-07-21): 90% say GenAI/agentic AI is transforming workflows, only 18% see significant revenue impact — the ROI-skepticism gap GitHub's new cohort dashboard is built to answer for sellers (vendor-commissioned survey, flagged)

title: Show HN: We stopped feature-gating our open source BI platform
summary: Helical Insight moved AI analytics, embedding, SSO, multi-tenancy and row-level security out of the paid tier into Community Edition, keeping a paid Enterprise edition (support, hosting, licensing) as the remaining revenue layer — a live data point for the feature-gating debate, though traction was minimal (1 pt, 0 comments)

title: Not just development, distribution of software may change as well
summary: Redis creator argues repos should ship as templates/examples for AI agents to adapt rather than polished, frozen releases — extends the "AI as a reader of your docs" thread to "AI as an editor of your repo"; watch for practitioner pushback

title: Show HN: OneCLI – OSS credential gateway that keeps secrets out of AI agents
summary: real Show HN traction (94 pts/29 comments) for infrastructure that keeps raw API keys away from agents, a second data point (after GoDaddy's agent-safe checkout) that "make the agent's actions safe by design" is becoming a buildable category, not just a guide bullet

title: Buyer intelligence goes headless: Common Room ships a `cr` CLI + MCP write-layer for AI agents, gated on identity resolution
summary: post-Zoom-acquisition, Common Room extends the "AI agent as actor" pattern past docs into GTM workflows (agents query/write buyer data without a UI), explicitly arguing agent-driven writes need a dedup/identity guardrail first ("reach without custody is just fast access to a mess"); cites Incident.io's vendor-claimed duplicate-account rate drop (3% → 0.3%, "70% reduction") from its DataAgent — a possible third data point for the agent-safe-by-design pattern (GoDaddy checkout, OneCLI credentials), though this is GTM/CRM data integrity, not security, so treat as adjacent texture, not a third confirming tool

title: Show HN: Axtary – content authorization for AI agents
summary: two same-day, thin-traction Show HNs (3 pts each) binding agent actions to pre-approved payloads/policy before execution; more texture for the "guardrail the agent's actions by design" thread (GoDaddy checkout, OneCLI credentials, Common Room identity resolution) but low signal on their own — volume of attempts is rising, proof of adoption still isn't
